newsitem.title: CANADA: Blackburn to sell some newspaper, radio assets.
newsitem.headline: Blackburn to sell some newspaper, radio assets.

text.p: Privately held Blackburn Group Inc said on Wednesday it decided to put most of its media assets on the block, including the London Free Press newspaper the Blackburn family has held for 148 years.
Assets for sale also included 75-year-old CFPL-AM and CFPL-FM radio, which was launched in 1948, the company said.
Blackburn said it also sought to sell Netmar, Canada's biggest publisher of weekly shopper publications, which are distributed to more than 1.6 million households in 25 Canadian cities.
"They make up the bulk of our media assets," Blackburn Media president Sandy Green said in a telephone interview.

He said the consolidation and the creation of large chains in the newspaper and radio industries made it tough for a relatively small independent operator to achieve economies of scale and stay competitive.
Conrad Black's Hollinger International Inc has a direct or indirect interest in about 40 percent of Canadian newspaper circulation through its own properties and its majority stake in Southam Inc.

Green said the company has not yet had any expressions of interest in the properties but chairman Bruce Pearson said in a statement that because of the strength of the assets offered, Blackburn expects "a significant industry response".
Blackburn will have eight satellite radio stations and Carfax, its U.S.-based data services unit which offers vehicle histories for cars across North America, after the sale.
The sale of Blackburn's broadcast assets will be managed by the company while the sale of its print and distribution units will be managed by T-D Securities.
